summary: With no subplan, the MS in Engineering is an individually proposed 45-unit program approved by a School of Engineering department: you move in the approved program's courses, and your advisor confirms that at least 21 of its units are letter-graded School of Engineering courses numbered 200 or above. The Biomechanical Engineering subplan instead needs two math courses in different areas, two approved life science or engineering electives, 21 units of graduate engineering courses including three biomechanical electives and a three-course specialty, and ME 389, with approved electives bringing these to 39 units and unrestricted electives to 45. Every course except the unrestricted electives must be letter graded where a letter grade is offered. Transfer units from other schools do not count.

mAbEGmbJ.why: "The MS in Engineering is available to current School of Engineering graduate students who develop specialized, interdisciplinary objectives that cannot conform to any graduate program offered at Stanford." A student in the Biomechanical Engineering subplan follows that program instead, so the individually proposed program is the path with no subplan. The block is required, not information: "There are three school requirements for the MS degree in Engineering".
